land.text: Dedan and Tayma: Lihyan 'fell into the hands of the Nabataeans around 65 BC' (some authors), annexed 'around 24 BC' (Caskel), with Dedan reached 'in 9 BC'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Nabataean shape of -164 already contains about 7,600 km2 of this circle; the Lihyan page's Nabataean annexation dates (65, 24 or 9 BC) are all later. The Lihyanites 'restored their independence under Han'as ibn Tilmi' after the Roman annexation of Nabatea in 106 AD (outside this dossier).

capitals.note: Infobox capital Dedan (al-Khuraybah, Al-'Ula oasis). Coordinates are those of AlUla, approximate, as the gazetteer has no place for it.

correction.text: the oasis kingdom round Dedan (al-Khuraybah, AlUla) with Tayma, 'ruled by Lihyanite kings'; no gazetteer place for AlUla or Tayma yet

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Lihyan; its Nabataean shapes from -164 and its Minaean shapes (-188, -170) touch the same oases. The page gives no area: it describes a domain 'from Yathrib (Medina) in the south to parts of the Levant in the north' and names AlUla, Dedan, Tayma and, among trade centres, Khaybar (not claimed for Lihyan). A 110 km circle round AlUla (about 34,000 km2, mostly desert) is the researcher's reading of the oasis core and should be drawn soft.

ledger.note: 6th century BC (bridged): the kingdom of Dadan stands at the AlUla oasis. 'Biblical accounts refer to Dadan as early as the sixth century BC' and Winnett places the start of the local dynasty 'in the 6th century BC'; the infobox gives the Dadanite phase as the 5th century BC. A century is not a year: the century's first year is used because Nabonidus ended the kings of Dadan c. 552 BC.

ledger.note: c. 552 BC: Nabonidus conquers Dedan and Tayma. 'Nabonidus swept through northwestern Arabia in c. 552 BC; eliminating the kings of both Tayma and Dadan' (Lihyan page); 'By March or April, Nabonidus had defeated the king of Dadanu, and had captured other cities in Arabia, including the city of Tayma, which he had established as a provisionary seat for himself by the summer of 552 BC' (Nabonidus page).

ledger.note: 543 BC: Nabonidus leaves Tayma. 'Nabonidus was in self-imposed exile in Tayma, Arabia from 552 to 543/542 BC'; 'October 543 BC is the return date most supported by surviving Babylonian documentation.'

c. 543 BC (bridged): the Lihyanite kingdom replaces the Dadanite. 'The Lihyanite kingdom most likely came into being after the arrival of Nabonidus in north-west Arabia in 552 BC'; Dedan 'served as the capital for two successive kingdoms'. Winnett has the Lihyanites 'appeared in the 4th century BC' and Rohmer and Charloux 'from the late 6th to the mid-3rd century BC': the page does not settle it. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: the oasis kingdom round Dedan (al-Khuraybah, AlUla) with Tayma, 'ruled by Lihyanite kings'; no gazetteer place for AlUla or Tayma yet

ledger.note: c. 24 BC: the Nabataeans annex Lihyan. 'The Nabataean annexation of Lihyan was around 24 BC' (Caskel); 'fell into the hands of the Nabataeans around 65 BC' (some authors); Aretas IV's inscription at Hegra is dated around 9 BC. Nabataean rule over Lihyan 'ended with the annexation of Nabatea by the Romans in 106 AD'.

ledger.note: c. 24 BC: the Lihyanite kingdom ends under the Nabataeans. The page's end for the kingdom itself is disputed: Winnett has it vanish in the 2nd century BC, Rohmer and Charloux in the mid-3rd century BC; the Nabataean annexation is the first date that is a political event.

sources.title: Lihyan
sources.note: Dadan then Lihyan, capital Dedan, Nabonidus c. 552 BC, the disputed dating of the Lihyanite kingdom (4th century, late 6th to mid-3rd), the Nabataean annexation (65, 24 or 9 BC), Han'as ibn Tilmi after 106 AD.

sources.title: Nabonidus
sources.note: May 553 BC departure, Dadanu and Tayma 553-552 BC, the exile 552-543/542 BC; Medina (Yatribu).

notes: Cliopatria has no Lihyan. The Lihyan page is deliberately unsettled on dating: 'at some point between the 5th and 1st centuries BC', Winnett's 4th-2nd centuries BC, Rohmer and Charloux's late 6th to mid-3rd centuries BC, and the Nabataean takeover at 65, 24 or 9 BC. This dossier keeps one state for the Dadanite and Lihyanite kingdoms (-600 to -24), with the Babylonian occupation 552-543 in between, and uses the dated events only; the real kingdom may have ended 150-250 years before the annexation, in which case Dedan was a Nabataean-sphere oasis for that gap. The minaeans dossier (me-04-c) has Ma'in's reach to Dedan in -170 and the page says only that Dedan 'hosted a community of Minaeans'. Gazetteer names needed: AlUla/Dedan, Tayma, Hegra (Mada'in Salih) as places. Han'as ibn Tilmi's restored Lihyan (after 106 AD) is not drawn. Page budget: two pages.
